hero.headline: Martin County Commissioner seeks to move Brightline station away from downtown Stuart
hero.body:
Martin County Commissioner Ed Ciampi has asked county staff to begin discussions with Brightline about relocating the planned train station from its current proposed location in downtown Stuart. The station was previously agreed to be built on a parking lot across from the courthouse in the downtown area. Ciampi suggested the fairgrounds as an alternative site, citing parking congestion and other issues at the downtown location as reasons to reconsider.

The commissioner's request comes in response to concerns raised by the FEC, which sent a letter to then-Stuart Mayor Christopher Collins stating it does not support a Brightline station in Stuart. According to the FEC, the proposed downtown station would violate U.S. Coast Guard rules because it would require the St. Lucie River Railroad bridge to remain lowered while the train stops at the station. Ciampi acknowledged that if the Army Corps of Engineers or U.S. Coast Guard determine the downtown location is too close to the bridge, the issue becomes moot for him. He argued that moving the station further south to the fairgrounds would eliminate the bridge proximity problem entirely.

The suggestion drew mixed responses from the community. Paul Gedwed, a resident, supported the idea, calling it a well-thought-out opinion given the congestion at the proposed downtown site. However, Steven Vitale, owner of the Colorado Inn, voiced concerns about moving the station away from downtown. He questioned why the county would build a train station that people cannot easily walk to, noting that most people would want to access downtown Stuart. Lisa Freitas, owner of Lisa Gay Fashion, expressed a different perspective, saying her downtown store would benefit either way the county decides, but urged officials to make a decision and proceed with the project regardless of location, as long as it remains in Martin County.

County officials clarified that Ciampi's comments do not constitute official direction for staff to implement changes. The board would need to formally discuss the relocation proposal and vote on it before staff could begin exploring alternative sites. Meanwhile, Martin County continues waiting for approval on its grant application to fund the Brightline station project. Until the funding is secured, the project cannot move forward with either location.

cards.headline: Portugal's national soccer team arrives in Palm Beach Gardens for World Cup training
cards.teaser: Portugal's national soccer team begins training Thursday at North County District Park in Palm Beach Gardens ahead of the World Cup, which kicks off Friday.
cards.body:
Portugal's national soccer team will arrive Thursday at North County District Park in Palm Beach Gardens to begin training ahead of the World Cup, which starts Friday. Media members covering Portugal's national team arrived Wednesday for a debriefing led by team intermediaries. Marco Carvalho, the media coordinator who has served in that role for three decades, told reporters the goal is to create a smooth experience for everyone involved during the World Cup. Carvalho said the Palm Beach Gardens setup compares favorably to other World Cup and European tournament venues he has experienced.

Portugal will train on fields adjacent to those England has been using for the past week at the complex. Tim Ford, sports and special facilities director for Palm Beach Gardens, said hosting England first helped the city prepare for Portugal's arrival. Ford said each team the city hosts helps staff learn what each team needs, and preparations continue to improve with each experience. Security will be extra tight around the facility when the team arrives. Ford said the city is putting final touches on the team's temporary home at the back end of the complex. Portugal has requested that video of the training center not be published until Saturday, allowing the team to have a first look at its first practice.

cards.headline: Lake Worth Beach advances downtown parking garage plan near K Street and First Avenue South
cards.teaser: Lake Worth Beach commissioners voted to advance a nearly $10 million proposal to build a four-and-a-half-story parking garage downtown, transforming an existing surface lot near K Street and First Avenue South.
cards.body:
A controversial proposal to build a new downtown parking garage in Lake Worth Beach is moving forward after a commission vote during a quasi-judicial hearing Monday night. The vote does not give final approval for construction. Instead, city leaders say it allows the project team to move forward with completing the garage's design and obtaining a guaranteed maximum price before construction can begin. The nearly $10 million proposal would transform an existing surface parking lot near K Street and First Avenue South into a four-and-a-half-story parking garage designed to add hundreds of parking spaces in the city's downtown core.

Vice Mayor Mimi May said the city has been talking about putting in a centralized parking area since the 1960s. May said the city has already seen potential business investment impacted by parking limitations, with businesses expressing interest in investing in Lake Worth Beach but unable to do so because the city could not accommodate parking for their needs. The proposed garage's location would provide easier access to downtown businesses than existing parking facilities located farther from the city's commercial core. A loan from WMODA of $3.5 million at 4 percent interest will be repaid in five years, with WMODA also paying $1 million towards the garage. May said everything has been already allocated and budgeted, so there will be no future payments coming from taxpayers. The proposal now heads to a second and final reading on June 30, with construction potentially moving forward and the garage opening as early as 2028.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County faces up to $324 million in losses if property tax reform passes
cards.teaser: Palm Beach County could lose $221 million in revenue in the first year if a Florida property tax reform referendum passes, with losses climbing to $324 million the following year.
cards.body:
Palm Beach County commissioners are grappling with this year's budget while preparing for potentially significant revenue losses if Florida voters approve a property tax reform referendum. The county could lose $221 million in revenue in the first year if the referendum passes, with losses climbing to $324 million the following year. Commissioner Maria Marino expressed the frustration many commissioners feel, saying "We're under attack with the property taxes." Commissioners are already under pressure to close a budget gap, with Commissioner Marci Woodward urging departments to find savings wherever possible.

A major point of discussion centered on the Palm Face County Sheriff's Office budget, which requests more than 8.5% more funding than last year. Commissioner Gregg Weiss noted that all new revenue dollars last year went to support the sheriff's budget needs, and this year it is all the new revenue dollars plus an additional $13 million. Lowering property taxes is part of a broader push by Gov. Ron DeSantis to make Florida more affordable. Commissioners were told that raising taxes on commercial and non-homestead properties, as well as increasing the millage rate, are possibilities. Commissioner Joel Flores said he would like to keep the millage rate at 4.5 for this year and then determine next steps for the following year. County commissioners maintain they have been running a tight operation on spending while acknowledging things could get much tighter ahead.

cards.headline: Riviera Beach pauses paid parking program at Ocean Walk and Singer Island after council member wrongfully cited
cards.teaser: Riviera Beach's paid parking program at Ocean Walk and Singer Island is temporarily on pause after Council Member Dr. Glen Spiritis was ticketed after driving into the parking lot and leaving without parking.
cards.body:
Riviera Beach's paid parking program at Ocean Walk and Singer Island is temporarily paused after Council Member Dr. Glen Spiritis was ticketed without ever parking. Mayor Douglas Lawson said Spiritis was charged after driving into the parking lot and immediately leaving. The pause was announced during last Wednesday's city council meeting. Lawson said the city has received an influx of concerns over the months since the program launched in October of last year. The program requires visitors to scan a QR code to pay for parking and has drawn complaints from business owners, customers and residents since its launch.

The pause is also a relief for Kerry Lutz, who filed a lawsuit challenging the program on the grounds that it violates federal standards. Lawson said the city will examine concerns related to handicap parking, timing and other issues, and will issue refunds to anyone who was wrongfully charged. Parking officials will bring back a full report on the program's fees and system. Lawson emphasized the pause is not permanent, stating the city will continue the system but is pausing to ensure it is done in the most effective and efficient way. He said the city needs to charge for parking to generate additional revenue but wants to do it correctly.

cards.headline: Delray Beach moves forward with e-bike safety ordinance after resident concerns
cards.teaser: City Commissioner Juli Casale moved forward with an e-bike safety ordinance Tuesday during a city commission meeting, citing safety concerns about kids on e-bikes buzzing around downtown Delray Beach.
cards.body:
City Commissioner Juli Casale moved forward with a safety ordinance for e-bikes during a city commission meeting Tuesday, citing concerns she has personally witnessed. "I just can't get over the number of kids I see buzzing around our downtown on those e-bikes, in front of cars, in front of pedestrians," Casale said. She emphasized that the city is not seeking to ban e-bikes but rather address unsafe riding behavior. "We just want the crazy behavior. I mean, someone is going to get hurt," Casale said.

The proposed ordinance could limit speeding and sidewalk riding, require IDs for riders, and mandate helmet use for those under 16 years old. The measure comes after several residents raised concerns about unsafe operations involving e-bikes and dirt bikes. City staff will draft the ordinance and present it at a future commission meeting for further consideration.

cards.headline: Palm Springs woman arrested after firing gun near family during road rage incident on Forest Hill Boulevard
cards.teaser: Jessica Piltz, 38, faces four counts of aggravated assault and discharging a firearm from a vehicle following a Sunday evening incident near the 4000 block of Forest Hill Boulevard.
cards.body:
Jessica Piltz, 38, was arrested Tuesday on four counts of aggravated assault and discharging a firearm from a vehicle following a road rage incident Sunday evening near the 4000 block of Forest Hill Boulevard, according to the Palm Springs Police Department. The incident began when a family was leaving McKenna's Place after dinner. The victim told police her parents had stopped their vehicle in the parking lot to help transfer a child's belongings between cars. Piltz was parked on the east side of the plaza and began backing out of her parking space, though witnesses told police Piltz was not blocked in and had adequate space to reverse. A family member moved their vehicle to give Piltz room.

After exiting her parking space, Piltz stopped her vehicle next to the family's car and began yelling at them. The victim repeatedly asked Piltz to leave. Piltz drove toward the plaza exit onto Kirk Road but stopped again and continued verbally assaulting the family. Piltz then drove north on Kirk Road, stopped her vehicle in the center turn lane and exited her car. Police reports indicate Piltz told the victim to "come get it" and "you are not about that life, I am." Piltz retrieved a firearm from her vehicle, inserted the magazine and charged the weapon. A witness stated Piltz partially sat in her vehicle with one leg out and fired a round in the family's direction before fleeing north on Kirk Road. Piltz is being held at the Palm Beach County Main Detention Center on $100,000 bond.

cards.headline: Singer Island beach littered with trash after Memorial Day weekend
cards.teaser: Overflowing trash cans, glass tequila bottles, styrofoam cups and beer cans were found on Singer Island just feet away from sea turtle nests following Memorial Day weekend.
cards.body:
WPTV found overflowing trash cans, glass tequila bottles, styrofoam cups and beer cans on Singer Island just feet away from sea turtle nests following the Memorial Day holiday. Beachgoer Stacie Safford expressed concern for the environment and sea turtles nesting nearby, saying "I am seeing the same thing you are seeing. A whole lot of garbage."

The city of Riviera Beach said in a statement it is aware of concerns about litter on the beach near Johnny Longboats following Memorial Day weekend. With higher-than-normal holiday attendance, beach activity increased significantly, resulting in more trash than usual. Parks and Recreation staff worked throughout the weekend with beach maintenance scheduled from 7 a.m., with Memorial Day coverage beginning at 6:30 a.m. Beach restrooms were cleaned three times during the weekend, including Monday, an increase from the usual two weekend cleanings. The city noted that during turtle season, sifting and combing are permitted only in limited beach areas to help protect sea turtle nests. Oceanside Beach Services assists with upkeep in designated service areas, including trash removal and seaweed clearing. The city said it will continue reviewing holiday operations and staffing levels to help keep Riviera Beach beaches clean, safe and enjoyable for residents and visitors.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County School Board raises safety concerns about AI data center near Saddle View Elementary
cards.teaser: The Palm Beach County School Board is raising significant safety and health concerns about a proposed artificial intelligence data center complex that would be built just 1,200 feet from Saddle View Elementary School.
cards.body:
The Palm Beach County School Board is raising significant safety and health concerns about Project Tango, a proposed hyperscale AI data center facility planned just 1,200 feet from Saddle View Elementary School. In a formal letter to Mayor Baxter and county commissioners during their June 3, 2026 meeting, School Board members outlined multiple potential risks to students and staff. These include industrial noise and vibrations that could disrupt the learning environment, environmental health impacts from facility operations, public safety risks including hazards from lithium battery fires, emergency response capabilities in the event of an incident, and infrastructure strain on local utilities and services.

The School Board is formally requesting access to any existing public records, impact studies, or reports the county has received regarding the project, specifically seeking information about potential noise levels, environmental impact assessments, public safety and emergency response planning, projected energy and water usage, and long-term economic effects on the community. While expressing these concerns, the School Board indicated a willingness to work with county officials if the project moves forward. They stated they hope to "work collaboratively with the Board of County Commissioners to identify and implement mitigation strategies" should Project Tango ultimately be approved.

hero.headline: Author explains soccer's growing appeal to American fans in new book
hero.teaser: Nick Greene, author of 'How to Watch Soccer Like a Genius,' believes Americans are embracing soccer more than many realize as the World Cup approaches.
hero.body:
Nick Greene, author of "How to Watch Soccer Like a Genius," believes Americans are embracing soccer far more than many people recognize. During a recent interview with WPTV's Jon Shainman, Greene shared his passion for the sport and discussed his book's unique approach to understanding the game. The book examines soccer through the perspectives of agronomists, architects, computer scientists, and other experts, offering readers fresh insights into why the sport captivates billions of fans worldwide. Greene emphasized soccer's fundamental appeal, saying "you have this game that is the simplest game, you just need a ball and you don't even need grass."

Several key moments in the 1990s transformed America's relationship with soccer. The 1994 World Cup, which took place in the United States, marked a turning point for the sport domestically. The launch of Major League Soccer that same decade provided American fans with a professional league to follow regularly. The 1999 U.S. Women's World Cup victory further energized public interest and demonstrated the sport's potential to capture American attention. These three milestones collectively contributed to soccer's sustained growth in the country over the past several decades.

The sport has undergone a dramatic evolution since its early days. Greene explained that soccer's transformation reflects a shift from individual-focused play to sophisticated team strategies. The first modern players, who emerged in England during the 1860s and 1870s, were aristocratic gentlemen who approached the game differently than today's professionals. One early player famously characterized the sport as something played "purely for my own pleasure," highlighting how individualistic the game once was. Modern soccer, by contrast, emphasizes complex tactical coordination and collective team objectives.

Looking toward the future, Greene contemplates soccer's next chapter in America. He questions whether the sport will maintain its current trajectory of steady growth or whether it will ascend to become a truly dominant spectacle in American culture, reaching what he calls "the stratosphere." Greene's expert-driven approach in his book aims to deepen readers' appreciation for soccer's tactical nuances and strategic elements. As the sport continues gaining momentum across the country, understanding these complexities becomes increasingly valuable for American audiences seeking to engage more fully with the game.

Beach restrooms were cleaned three times during the weekend, including Monday, an increase from the usual two weekend cleanings. The city noted that during turtle season, sifting and combing are permitted only in limited beach areas to protect sea turtle nests. Oceanside Beach Services assists with upkeep in designated service areas, including trash removal and seaweed clearing where beach chairs are set up.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County faces $324 million loss if property tax reform passes
cards.teaser: Palm Beach County commissioners are bracing for significant revenue losses as they work on this year's budget while Florida voters consider a property tax reform referendum.
cards.body:
Palm Beach County commissioners are wrestling with this year's budget while bracing for potential revenue losses if Florida voters approve a property tax reform referendum. The county could lose $221 million in revenue in the first year if the referendum passes, with losses climbing to $324 million the following year. Commissioner Maria Marino expressed the sentiment many are feeling, saying "We're under attack with the property taxes." Commissioners are already under pressure to close a budget gap. Commissioner Marci Woodward called on departments to find savings wherever possible, stating "Any departments that can bring us lower numbers, because they found a different source, I would like to say thank you and keep working on that."

A major point of discussion was the Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office budget, which includes a request for more than 8.5% more funding than last year. Commissioner Gregg Weiss noted that last year all new revenue dollars went to support the sheriff's office needs, and this year it's all the new revenue dollars plus an additional $13 million. Lowering property taxes is part of a broader push by Governor Ron DeSantis to make Florida more affordable. Commissioners were told that raising taxes on commercial and non-homestead properties, as well as increasing the millage rate, are possibilities. Commissioner Joel Flores said he would like to keep the millage rate at 4.5 for this year and then figure out where to go next year because things will be chaotic.

hero.headline: Delray Beach Public Library offers free summer STREAM programs, daily lunches for kids and teens
hero.body:
The Delray Beach Public Library is brightening summer for local kids and teens by offering free STREAM programs covering Science, Technology, Reading, Art, Engineering and Math. All Florida residents can participate in activities at the library's 36,000-square-foot facility located at Atlantic Avenue and Swinton Avenue in downtown Delray Beach. According to Kae Jonsons, director of development and community relations, the library has a long history of serving the community. It was founded in 1913 when 30 women from the Ladies Improvement Society each donated a book to start the collection. The library now welcomes more than 193,000 visitors annually.

Young adult librarian Natalie Baron is leading sessions designed for teens, including ColorSpace: Artistic Excavations, where participants explore art history spanning from cave paintings to ancient pottery. Teens can also participate in lab-based activities like collaborative 3D puzzle builds and select themed book boxes. Mandy Fulop, head of the children's department, launched the STREAM Into Summer Literacy Program to help young readers set goals with librarians and track their progress. Participants take home an Unearth a Story bag containing a free STREAM book and related activities. Those interested can register at delraylibrary.org.

Working with the School District of Palm Beach County, the library provides free lunch daily from 11:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m. and snacks from 2 p.m. to 4 p.m. to youth up to age 18. Family Nights on select Tuesdays invite children age 5 and older to explore STREAM topics together. The library also runs Saturday Science Discovery programs for ages 9 to 12 that feature hands-on archaeology activities including "Piece Together History," trash bag archaeology, carbon dating, and fossil hunts.

Upcoming special events include visits from Malachi Fenn of the Florida Public Archaeology Network on June 11, a Sea Turtle Adventures beach cleanup on June 25, American Shark Conservancy's SharkSmarts presentation on July 2, and FPAN's Beyond Artifacts program on July 16. The library's free, high-quality education programs help bridge summer learning gaps while keeping families engaged and promoting community connections in an accessible, safe space within walking distance for many residents. A complete program lineup and registration details for each event are available at delraylibrary.org.

cards.headline: Cornell Art Museum in Delray Beach opens Persistence of Matter exhibit featuring upcycled art through September
cards.teaser: The Cornell Art Museum at Old School Square has opened Persistence of Matter, a summer exhibition spotlighting artists who turn discarded materials into sculptures, installations, and mixed media pieces.
cards.body:
The Cornell Art Museum at Old School Square has opened Persistence of Matter, an exhibition featuring artists who transform discarded materials into sculptures, installations, and mixed media pieces. According to Delray Beach Downtown Development Authority Cultural Arts Director Marusca Gatto, the show aligns with the museum's mission to merge creativity with community impact. Guest curators Mavis Benson and Pamela Lambie selected featured artists including Autumn Kioti, whose work draws on natural and urban influences, and Mike Silverman. Silverman's Self-Reflection series uses discarded hard drive platters and printed circuit boards to create reflective sculptures. "Every piece invites viewers to see themselves and their relationship to technology and waste in a new light," Silverman said.

The exhibition runs through September 10, 2026, and offers special programs including artist talks, salon discussions, and film screenings. The museum is open Wednesday from noon to 5 p.m., Thursday and Friday from noon to 7 p.m., Saturday from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m., and Sunday from noon to 5 p.m. For event details, call 561-654-2220.

hero.headline: Byron Donalds holds 46-point lead in Florida GOP gubernatorial primary, new poll shows
hero.body:
Congressman Byron Donalds is dominating the Republican primary race for Florida governor, according to a new poll from the Associated Industries of Florida. The survey shows Donalds capturing 54 percent support among Republican primary voters, giving him a 46-point advantage over his nearest competitor. Conducted June 3-7 among 386 Republican primary voters, the poll found James Fishback at 8 percent, Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins at 5 percent, and former House Speaker Paul Renner at 2 percent. Nearly a third of respondents, 31 percent, remain undecided about the race.

Donalds demonstrates strong support across Florida's major population centers and demographic groups. In Fort Myers, he leads with 71 percent support, followed by 69 percent in West Palm Beach, 54 percent in Orlando, 53 percent in the Panhandle, and 51 percent in Tampa. Among white Republicans, Donalds draws 55 percent support, while earning 54 percent among Hispanic Republicans. Senior voters, who typically show the highest participation rates in primary elections, back Donalds at 60 percent. These results align with previous polling data showing his consistent strength. An Emerson College survey in April found Donalds at 46 percent in the primary, with Collins and Fishback each at 4 percent.

Donalds enters the primary race with significant financial and political advantages. He has raised more than 81 million dollars through his campaign and the Friends of Byron Donalds PAC from over 35,000 donors. He also carries the complete endorsement of President Donald Trump. The campaign has constructed an extensive field apparatus throughout Florida to prepare for early voting, which begins in two months. An April poll by Echelon Insights showed Donalds leading Democrat David Jolly 49 percent to 43 percent in a potential general election matchup.

Jeremy Sheftel, AIF vice president of Political Operations, said the polling demonstrates Donalds' commanding position heading into the primary. Ryan Smith, the campaign's chief strategist, emphasized that Florida Republicans are uniting behind Donalds and his message about making the state more affordable. Smith characterized Donalds as a common sense conservative who will defeat liberal candidates. The primary election is scheduled for August 18, with the Republican and Democratic nominees advancing to the November 3 general election. The Associated Industries of Florida will present the full poll findings at its Summer Political and Policy Retreat in Sarasota.

cards.headline: Entire Florida Senate Democratic Caucus endorses Ashley Gantt for Senate District 34
cards.teaser: All 12 members of the Florida Senate Democratic Caucus have united behind former teacher and attorney Ashley Gantt in her bid for Senate District 34, her campaign announced Thursday.
cards.body:
Ashley Gantt's Senate District 34 campaign has secured the endorsement of the entire Florida Senate Democratic Caucus, adding five new supporters to the seven who backed her last week. The new endorsers include Senate Democratic Leader-Designate Tracie Davis, Senator Shevrin Jones whose seat Gantt is seeking, and Senators Kristen Arrington, Brian Nathan and Darryl Rouson. Jones, who represented the Miami Gardens-area district before launching a run for Florida's 24th Congressional District, said the choice in SD 34 is clear. Davis called Gantt "exactly the kind of leader our caucus needs and exactly the kind of Senator South Florida deserves," citing her as principled and deeply connected to constituents. The full caucus endorsement also includes Senate Democratic Leader Lori Berman and Senators Mack Bernard, LaVon Bracy Davis, Carlos Guillermo Smith, Rosalind Osgood, Tina Polsky and Barbara Sharief.

Gantt won her House District 109 seat in 2022 by fewer than 500 votes and secured re-election two years later by 24 percentage points. She has raised nearly $27,000 and spent close to $7,000 this cycle through her campaign account. Three others are running for SD 34: Democrat Shanna Ighodaro, Republican Elizabeth Jeanty and no-party candidate Francisco Amador. Senate District 34 covers portions of northeast Miami-Dade, including Bay Harbor Islands, Miami Beach, North Miami, North Miami Beach, Opa-locka and Miami Gardens. The primary election is scheduled for August 18, followed by the general election on November 3.

cards.headline: Former Florida CFO Alex Sink endorses Leela Gray for 13th Congressional District
cards.teaser: Former Florida Chief Financial Officer Alex Sink is backing Democrat Leela Gray for Florida's 13th Congressional District, giving the retired Army Brigadier General another high-profile supporter.
cards.body:
Former Florida Chief Financial Officer Alex Sink has endorsed Democrat Leela Gray for Florida's 13th Congressional District. Sink, who served as CFO before becoming the Democratic nominee for Governor in 2010, founded Ruth's List Florida. "She spent more than 30 years earning every promotion, managing complex missions, and never once putting herself before the people she served," Sink said. "That kind of fiscal discipline and accountability is exactly what we need in Washington right now." The endorsement adds to Gray's growing institutional support, which includes backing from U.S. Representative Ben Diamond, U.S. Representative Kathy Castor, Safety Harbor Mayor Joe Ayoub, EMILY's List, New Politics and VoteVets. Gray's campaign raised $100,000 in the 10 days after Governor Ron DeSantis approved the new congressional map.

Gray is a third-generation veteran, attorney and small business leader who served more than 30 years in uniform, including two combat deployments and a peacekeeping mission. She retired in 2018 as Deputy Commanding General of U.S. Army Central and later advised U.S. Army Cyber Command on national cyber policy modernization. She earned a law degree to help veterans access health care and benefits. As of early Thursday morning, Gray, incumbent Anna Paulina Luna and Democrat Brandt Robinson had qualified for the race. The primary election is scheduled for August 18, with party nominees advancing to the November 3 general election.

cards.headline: Former Congressman Alan Grayson enters race for Florida's 7th Congressional District
cards.teaser: Former Democratic Congressman Alan Grayson has jumped into the race to challenge U.S. Representative Cory Mills in Florida's 7th Congressional District, which stretches from suburbs northeast of Orlando to South Daytona and New Smyrna Beach.
cards.body:
Former Democratic Congressman Alan Grayson is the latest candidate to challenge U.S. Rep. Cory Mills in Florida's 7th Congressional District. Grayson was first elected to Congress in 2008, representing Florida's 8th Congressional District. He was defeated after a single term, but won election in 2012 in the 9th Congressional District and served two more terms. In 2016, Grayson opted not to run for re-election and launched an unsuccessful Senate campaign, losing the Democratic primary to Patrick Murphy. He has since announced his candidacy for and dropped out of the 2022 U.S. Senate race and lost Democratic primaries for Florida's 10th Congressional District and Florida Senate Districts 15 and 25. Last year, he filed to run for the 2026 U.S. Senate Special Election but did not qualify.

Grayson joins former Navy nuclear reactor plant supervisor Marialana Kinter and Navy aviator Bale Dalton in the Democratic primary. Through the end of March, Dalton reported raising $692,000, while Kinter has raised $334,000. The Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee has identified Mills' seat as a top target for taking back the House and has endorsed Dalton. President Donald Trump carried the district by 13 percentage points in 2024, but in January, Cook Political Report changed the district's rating from Safe Republican to Likely Republican. The Office of Congressional Ethics concluded that 94 government contracts have been awarded to entities owned by Mills since January 2024. In November 2025, the House Ethics Committee formed an investigative subcommittee to examine fraud allegations against Mills and two alleged incidents involving his conduct toward women. Primary election day is August 18.

cards.headline: Democrat Jose Javier Rodriguez criticizes Attorney General Uthmeier over Jacksonville probes
cards.teaser: Democratic Attorney General candidate Jose Javier Rodriguez said Thursday his opponent James Uthmeier does not respect home rule and Jacksonville's ability to govern itself without interference from the state's chief legal officer.
cards.body:
Democrat José Javier Rodríguez criticized Attorney General James Uthmeier's handling of two Jacksonville issues on Thursday, saying the attorney general is overstepping his authority. Rodríguez, a former state representative, state senator, and Assistant Secretary of Labor for Employment and Training of the United States, said Uthmeier has focused on a log book of gun owners entering city buildings and JEA's decision to part ways with Ballard Partners. Regarding the gun registry, Uthmeier is suing the city for $5 million, the maximum penalty under state law, claiming the city willfully kept an illegal gun registry. However, Rodríguez noted that State Attorney Melissa Nelson absolved Jacksonville Mayor Donna Deegan's office of criminal liability, determining that it was not intentional but rather a mistake. Rodríguez said Uthmeier was invoking a remedial statute that allows for the destruction of records.

On the JEA probe, Rodríguez suggested Uthmeier was favoring Ballard Partners, the lobbying firm that employs former Mayor Lenny Curry and Chief of Staff Jordan Elsbury. Uthmeier has requested records from Deegan and key staffer Mike Weinstein discussing the arrangement between the city's independent utility and the lobbying firm. Rodríguez said everything surrounding the probes is hyperpartisan and hyperpolitical, calling Uthmeier's actions bullying without clear legal backing.

cards.headline: Florida CFO Blaise Ingoglia qualifies for ballot with more than $6 million in campaign funds
cards.teaser: State CFO and Fire Marshal Blaise Ingoglia, appointed last year by Governor Ron DeSantis, has qualified for his first statewide ballot test with more than $6 million in total campaign resources.
cards.body:
The Spring Hill Republican raised more than $168,000 to his campaign account in April and May from 199 contributions, pushing the total brought in to nearly $1.15 million. He spent nearly $42,500 during the same period and retained roughly $940,000 in campaign cash as of May 31. The Friends of Blaise Ingoglia account saw the most activity during April and May, with more than $305,000 brought in. The committee carries nearly $4.4 million as of the latest report. Of the 54 donors during the two-month fundraising period, nearly a third were in construction, real estate, or the roofing industry.

Ingoglia's Government Gone Wild PAC accrued more than $6,300 in interest charges during April and May, with no other fundraising to the account. Even with $70,000 of outflows, the committee closed May with nearly $1.2 million to spend. As CFO, Ingoglia has driven Florida Agency for Fiscal Accountability audits of local governments throughout the state and traveled from town to town to spotlight how spending has spiked since the pandemic. Qualified opponents include Republican Frank Collige of Glen St. Mary, who has almost $11,000 to spend, and Democrat Earle Ford, who redesignated from Florida's 13th Congressional District after raising $44,000 for that bid. Annette Taddeo of Miami opened a campaign account on June 5 and has yet to qualify.

cards.headline: Robin Peguero tops $900,000 in fundraising for Florida's 27th Congressional District
cards.teaser: Former Miami homicide prosecutor Robin Peguero has now raised $900,000 toward flipping Florida's 27th Congressional District, his campaign announced, adding roughly $100,000 to the $820,000 he reported at the start of the second quarter.
cards.body:
Robin Peguero has raised $900,000 for Florida's 27th Congressional District race, his campaign announced. The former Miami homicide prosecutor and ex-congressional investigator collected contributions from nearly 6,500 individual donors with no corporate PAC money or self-loans. According to his campaign, he has outraised his lone Democratic primary opponent nearly 2 to 1. Official fundraising numbers for the April 1 through June 30 period are due July 15. The qualifying period for state, congressional and county races closes Friday.

Peguero faces former Miami television news anchor Eliott Rodriguez in the Democratic primary for CD 27, which includes Miami, Coral Gables, Cutler Bay, Key Biscayne, Pinecrest, North Bay Village, South Miami, West Miami and several unincorporated Miami-Dade communities. His endorsement list includes the Congressional Hispanic Caucus BOLD PAC, the Congressional Black Caucus PAC, Latino Victory Fund and U.S. Representative Lois Frankel. The Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee identified CD 27 as one of three Florida congressional districts considered in play this cycle. The primary election is scheduled for August 18, followed by the general election on November 3.

cards.headline: Singer Island beach left with overflowing trash after Memorial Day weekend
cards.teaser: Riviera Beach officials say beach attendance increased significantly over Memorial Day weekend, resulting in more trash than usual at Singer Island.
cards.body:
Singer Island beach was left littered with overflowing trash cans, glass tequila bottles, styrofoam cups and beer cans following Memorial Day weekend, with debris found just feet away from sea turtle nests near Johnny Longboats. Beachgoer Stacie Safford expressed concern about the trash and its impact on the environment and nesting sea turtles.

Riviera Beach officials said higher-than-normal holiday attendance resulted in increased beach activity and more trash than usual. Parks and Recreation staff worked throughout the weekend, with beach maintenance scheduled starting at 7 a.m. and Memorial Day coverage beginning at 6:30 a.m. Daily assignments included opening restrooms, emptying trash receptacles, clearing sand from showers, sidewalks, pavilions and playgrounds, and servicing trash cans along beach access points. Beach restrooms were cleaned three times during the weekend, an increase from the usual two weekend cleanings. The city noted that during turtle season, sifting and combing are permitted only in limited beach areas to protect sea turtle nests. Oceanside Beach Services assists with upkeep in designated service areas, including trash removal and seaweed clearing where beach chairs are set up. The city said it will continue reviewing holiday operations and staffing levels to keep beaches clean and safe.

cards.headline: Riviera Beach pauses paid parking program after council member wrongfully ticketed
cards.teaser: Riviera Beach has temporarily paused its paid parking program at Ocean Walk and Singer Island after Council Member Dr. Glen Spiritis was ticketed without ever parking.
cards.body:
Riviera Beach's paid parking program at Ocean Walk and Singer Island is temporarily on pause after a city council member was ticketed without ever parking. Mayor Douglas Lawson says Council Member Dr. Glen Spiritis was charged for driving into the parking lot and immediately leaving. The pause was announced during last Wednesday's city council meeting. Lawson said the city has received an influx of concerns over the months since the program launched in October of last year. The program requires visitors to scan a QR code to pay for parking and has drawn complaints from business owners, customers and residents since its launch.

Lawson said parking officials will bring back a full report on the program's fees and system. The mayor said the city will look at all concerns regarding handicap parking and timing, with any issues addressed accordingly. The city will issue refunds to anybody who was wrongfully charged. Lawson emphasized the pause is not permanent and the city will continue the system but wants to ensure it is done in the most effective and efficient way. He stated the city needs to charge for parking to generate additional revenue but wants to do it the right way.

cards.headline: Delray Beach moves forward with e-bike safety ordinance after resident concerns
cards.teaser: Delray Beach City Commissioner Juli Casale moved forward with an e-bike safety ordinance during a city commission meeting Tuesday, citing safety concerns witnessed firsthand.
cards.body:
Delray Beach could soon have new rules governing e-bikes after City Commissioner Juli Casale moved forward with a safety ordinance during a city commission meeting Tuesday. Casale cited safety concerns she has witnessed firsthand, noting the number of children riding e-bikes in downtown Delray Beach in front of cars and pedestrians. "I just can't get over the number of kids I see buzzing around our downtown on those e-bikes, in front of cars, in front of pedestrians," Casale said.

The proposed ordinance could limit speeding and sidewalk riding, require IDs for riders, and push for helmet use for those under 16 years old. Casale said several residents have raised concerns about unsafe operations from e-bikes and dirt bikes. She emphasized that the goal is not to stop people from using e-bikes but to address dangerous behavior. "We're not looking to stop people from utilizing them. We just want the crazy behavior. I mean, someone is going to get hurt," Casale said. City staff will draft the ordinance and present it at a later commission meeting.

hero.headline: Operation Summer Heat results in 24 arrests and 7 firearms recovered in St. Lucie County
hero.teaser: A law enforcement crackdown in St. Lucie County has led to two dozen arrests and the seizure of multiple firearms.
hero.body:
A law enforcement crackdown called Operation Summer Heat has led to 24 arrests and the seizure of 7 firearms across St. Lucie County. The initiative is part of ongoing efforts by police to address criminal activity in the region during the summer months. One recent case illustrates the types of incidents the operation targets.

A Port St. Lucie man was arrested following a road rage incident involving a pregnant driver. Robert Kniceley, 78, was driving a yellow Chevrolet pickup truck east on St. Lucie West Boulevard on a Tuesday afternoon when he began honking and driving aggressively. At the intersection of SW Peacock Boulevard and SW St. Lucie West Boulevard, he pulled alongside the victim's vehicle. When she rolled down her window, he allegedly pointed a handgun at her. The woman, who is in late pregnancy, became frightened for her safety and called 911.

Police responded and obtained video evidence the victim recorded of Kniceley leaving the area. Officers traced his license plate to his residence, where they recovered a loaded Smith Wesson .22 caliber handgun with a round in the chamber. During the investigation, Kniceley told authorities that the victim had cut him off on the roadway, causing him to become angry. He was charged with aggravated assault with a deadly weapon and transported to St. Lucie County Jail. A risk protection order seizure process was also initiated as part of the investigation.

Officer Brittany Holly with the Port St. Lucie Police Department emphasized the importance of avoiding escalation during traffic conflicts. "It's not worth the argument, it's not worth the fight," Holly said. "Disengage from that, allow room for that individual who clearly is upset or angry at whatever reason to get away, and you can safely get to a police station, a fire station." The message reflects law enforcement's broader approach to reducing violence during summer months when communities see increases in activity and tensions on roadways.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie man arrested for pointing loaded gun at pregnant driver during road rage incident
cards.teaser: Robert Kniceley, 78, of Port St.
cards.body:
Robert Kniceley, 78, of Port St. Lucie was arrested and charged with aggravated assault with a deadly weapon after police say he pointed a loaded gun at a pregnant driver during a road rage incident Tuesday afternoon. According to Port St. Lucie police, Kniceley was driving a yellow Chevrolet pickup truck east on St. Lucie West Boulevard when he began honking and driving aggressively near the victim's vehicle. He pulled up alongside her vehicle at the intersection of SW Peacock Boulevard and SW St. Lucie West Boulevard, and when she rolled down her window, he allegedly pointed a handgun at her. The victim, who is in the late stages of pregnancy, became scared for her safety.

Police traced Kniceley's license plate to his residence, where they recovered a loaded Smith & Wesson .22 caliber handgun with a round in the chamber. The victim provided video evidence of Kniceley leaving the area and made a 911 call describing the incident. Police say Kniceley told investigators the victim cut him off on the roadway, causing him to become enraged. Kniceley was transported to St. Lucie County Jail, and a risk protection order seizure process was initiated as part of the investigation. Officer Brittany Holly with the Port St. Lucie Police Department advised disengaging from such incidents and safely reaching a police station or fire station.

cards.headline: Brightline station location debate divides Martin County community
cards.teaser: Martin County Commissioner Ed Ciampi called for discussions about moving the planned Brightline station away from downtown Stuart.
cards.body:
Martin County Commissioner Ed Ciampi called on county staff to open discussions with Brightline leadership about potentially moving the planned train station from its previously agreed-upon downtown Stuart location. Brightline and the county had previously agreed the station would be built on a parking lot site across from the courthouse in downtown Stuart. Ciampi suggested revisiting the fairgrounds as an alternative site. His comments came after the FEC sent a letter to then-Stuart mayor Christopher Collins explaining it does not support a Brightline station in Stuart, stating the proposed station violates U.S. Coast Guard rules because it would require the St. Lucie River Railroad bridge to remain down while the train stops at the station.

Community members expressed mixed reactions to Ciampi's proposal. Steven Vitale, owner of the Colorado Inn, argued for keeping the station downtown, saying "Most of the people are going to want to go to downtown Stuart, so why would we want to build a train station that people can't walk to." However, resident Paul Gedwed supported relocating the station, citing congestion concerns at the proposed location. Lisa Freitas, owner of Lisa Gay Fashion, said her downtown store will benefit regardless of the station's location. The county clarified that Ciampi's comments are not official direction for staff and the topic would need to return to the board for discussion and vote before action can be taken. The county is still waiting to hear back on its grant application to fund the Brightline station.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County faces up to $324 million in losses from Florida property tax reform
cards.teaser: Palm Beach County could lose hundreds of millions in revenue if Florida voters approve a property tax reform referendum.
cards.body:
Palm Beach County commissioners are wrestling with this year's budget while bracing for significant potential revenue losses if Florida voters approve a property tax reform referendum. Estimates show the county could lose $221 million in revenue in the first year if the referendum passes, with losses climbing to $324 million the following year. Commissioner Maria Marino captured the sentiment many are feeling, saying "We're under attack with the property taxes."

Commissioners are already under pressure to close a budget gap, with Commissioner Marci Woodward calling on departments to find savings wherever possible. A major point of discussion was the Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office budget, which includes a request for more than 8.5% more funding than last year. According to Commissioner Gregg Weiss, all new revenue dollars plus an additional $13 million would go toward the sheriff's budget. Lowering property taxes is part of a broader push by Gov. Ron DeSantis to make Florida more affordable. Commissioners were told that raising taxes on commercial and non-homestead properties, as well as increasing the millage rate, are possibilities. County commissioners insist they have been running a tight ship on spending and acknowledge things could get much tighter in the years ahead.

cards.headline: Woman arrested after firing gun near family in Palm Springs road rage incident
cards.teaser: Jessica Piltz, 38, faces four counts of aggravated assault after firing a weapon during a road rage incident Sunday evening.
cards.body:
Jessica Piltz, 38, was arrested Tuesday on four counts of aggravated assault and discharging a firearm from a vehicle following a road rage incident Sunday evening near the 4000 block of Forest Hill Boulevard in Palm Springs, according to the Palm Springs Police Department. The incident began when a family was leaving McKenna's Place after dinner. Piltz was parked on the east side of the plaza and began backing out of her parking space. After exiting her parking space, Piltz stopped her vehicle next to the family's car and began yelling at them. The victim repeatedly asked Piltz to leave.

Piltz drove toward the plaza exit onto Kirk Road but stopped again and continued verbally assaulting the family before driving north on Kirk Road. She then stopped her vehicle in the center turn lane and exited her car. According to police reports, Piltz retrieved a firearm from her vehicle, inserted the magazine and charged the weapon while telling the victim to "come get it" and "you are not about that life, I am." A witness stated Piltz partially sat in her vehicle with one leg out and fired a round in the family's direction before fleeing north on Kirk Road. Piltz is being held at the Palm Beach County Main Detention Center on $100,000 bond.
